args.text: Typing a file name into GitHub's search usually returns results from every public repository, which is rarely what you want. There is a way to keep the search inside the project you are already looking at.

args.name: type / to search
args.instruction: Open the search from a repository page, not from the GitHub home page. That is what limits the results.

args.text: Opened this way, the search box already contains a filter naming this repository. Everything you type is added to that filter rather than replacing it.

args.name: Search or jump to
args.instruction: The repo: prefix was filled in for you. Leave it in place and type after it.

args.name: Search or jump to
args.instruction: Type what you are looking for after the filter - a word from the code, not a file name.

args.text: The results come only from this project. The same filter works for issues and pull requests.

args.title: Open it with one key
args.description: On any repository page, the slash key opens the same search.

args.text: Press slash on a repository page, and the search opens with the filter already in place.

finish.openingSubtitle: GitHub · code search in one project
finish.closingText: Every search you start from a repository now stays inside it.
